extracted.intended_audience: expectant parents or anyone evaluating the suitability of the baby name 'Robert'
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and presenting the given name Robert for prospective parents, including meaning, origin, pronunciation, popularity, variations, famous bearers, and pairing suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning and origin
rubrics_metrics.description: The name Robert is of Old English origin and means "bright fame." It derives from the German name Hrodebert; composed of hrōd "renown" + berht "bright", "famous."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the etymology and literal elements (hrōd + berht) to explain semantic connotations. Note historical introduction (introduced to Britain by the Normans) and the name's royal/status associations (borne by kings, saints, noblemen).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender, syllables, and pronunciation
rubrics_metrics.description: Gender: Male. Syllables: 2. Pronunciation: rah-bert. The page labels the name as Masculine and Rare (top metadata).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear gender labeling, syllable count, and a simple pronunciation guide for readers. Include any site-level metadata (e.g., "Masculine", frequency labels like "Rare").

rubrics_metrics.name: Popularity (historical and recent)
rubrics_metrics.description: According to the Social Security Administration data, the name Robert has been a stalwart in terms of popularity over decades, consistently ranking within the top names for boys; it has seen a gradual decline in rankings over recent years but still remains a popular choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report SSA trends and changes over time; mention current-year changes (the page shows a percent change indicator such as "- 6% this year"). Provide geographic popularity (map by U.S. state) when available to show regional differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variations and diminutives
rubrics_metrics.description: List of variations includes Berto, Burto, Robbi, Robbie, Robbee, Robby, Roberto, Rupert, Rubert, Robertson, Robin, Robinson, Robbins, Robben, Riobard, Robey, Rober, Rab, Rob, Bobby, Bob, Bert, Berty, Tito, Dob, Dobbs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present a comprehensive set of formal variants, diminutives, and anglicized forms so parents can see shorter/nickname options and related names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nicknames
rubrics_metrics.description: Common shortened names: Bob, Bobby, Rob, Robby.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight familiar nicknames separately from formal variations; suggest how nicknames might influence everyday usage and perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notable historical and contemporary bearers
rubrics_metrics.description: Famous people listed with this first name include Robert Blake, Robert De Niro, Robert Downey Jr., Robert Kelly, Robert Redford, Robert Rodriguez, Robert Wagner, plus historical figures like Robert the Bruce, Robert Frost, and Robert Hooke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use examples of well-known real people to illustrate the name's cultural resonance across fields (arts, science, royalty). Note how famous bearers can shape associations and perceived prestige.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pop culture and fictional associations
rubrics_metrics.description: Fictional characters include Robert Baratheon (Game of Thrones), Robert Langdon (The Da Vinci Code), Robert Chase (House M.D.), Robert Neville (I Am Legend), and Robert "Rocky" Balboa (Rocky).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List prominent fictional Roberts and provide a short descriptor of each character to communicate narrative associations (e.g., king, symbologist, doctor, survivor, boxer). Consider how these associations affect name image.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family name origins & surname usage
rubrics_metrics.description: As a family name: English, French, German, Dutch, Hungarian (Róbert), etc; sometimes an Americanized form of like-sounding Jewish surnames. Historical records cite Roberts in various colonial records with secondary surnames.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the personal name functions as a surname in different cultures, including common secondary surnames and migration/record examples that demonstrate surname usage and variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethnic and language variations
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethnic/linguistic variations noted: English, French, German, Dutch, Hungarian (Róbert) and other forms across Europe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document cross-linguistic variants and spelling/pronunciation differences for multicultural families or those seeking ethnic variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Middle name pairing suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested middle names that pair well with Robert: Arthur, Christopher, Daniel, Hayden, Sterling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer curated middle-name pairings to help parents choose full names that match style/tone; provide several options spanning traditional to more modern choices.
